  # Notebook Navigator: metadata-related features
  
  ## Sources read
  - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/johansan/notebook-navigator/main/README.md (read in two parts: offset 0 and offset 39914)
  - https://notebooknavigator.com/docs.html (docs site copy of the README, with slightly different section numbers)
  - https://notebooknavigator.com/ (marketing landing page)
  - https://github.com/johansan/notebook-navigator/wiki (Home page only; it links a "Custom CSS" page, which I did not read)
  - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/johansan/notebook-navigator/main/docs/api-reference.md
  
  Not read: the other docs/ files (startup-process, metadata-pipeline, storage-architecture, rendering-architecture, and the rest), FAQ.md, and the wiki's Custom CSS page.
  
  ## Version
  - No plugin version number appears in the README or the docs site. These describe the current `main` branch, not a tagged release.
  - The README badge requires Obsidian v1.13.0+.
  - The API reference is "Current API Version: 2.0.0" (changelog entry dated 2026-03-07). The page was last updated July 1, 2026.
  - The wiki Home page was last edited September 18, 2026.
  
  ## Feature-by-feature (metadata use)
  
  **Frontmatter properties and the Properties section**
  - Property browser: "Browse file properties organized by key and value with file counts, custom colors, icons, and drag and drop." It is a navigation-pane tree, like tags.
  - Search: `.key` matches keys starting with "key"; `.key=value` matches values containing "value"; `."Reading Status"="In Progress"` for keys and values with spaces. Exclusions use `-.key` and `-.key=value`. `.key=null` matches a key that exists with no value.
  - Cmd/Ctrl+Click a property adds it with AND; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Click adds it with OR.
  - Commands: "Navigate to property" (search dialog over keys and values), "Toggle properties by selection" (limits properties to those in the selected folder or tag), "Set property on selected files".
  - Property grouping (list pane): groups notes by a frontmatter value, matching Obsidian Bases group-by. Notes without the property fall into a trailing "None" group. Groups use natural sort.
  - Custom properties in the file list: "Display frontmatter properties or word count in file list with per-folder/tag overrides and custom colors." The exact UI setting name is not given.
  - Frontmatter for names and timestamps: "Read note names and timestamps from frontmatter fields." The docs use the setting "Name fields" under Frontmatter (set to `title` in the example). Other date fields are described only under the search note below.
  
  **Tags**
  - Tag tree: "Hierarchical tags with configurable root tag ordering." Drag-and-drop reparenting. Commands "Toggle tag sort order" (alphabetical vs frequency) and "Toggle tags by selection" (limits tags to those in the selected folder or property).
  - Tag operations: "Add/remove/clear tags, rename/delete tags, create note in tag."
  - Tags in the file list are clickable and navigate to that tag.
  - Search: `#tag` also matches nested children (`#tag/subtag`); `#` means tagged only; `-#` means untagged only; `#a OR #b AND #c` gives AND precedence.
  - Virtual tag collections: the API has aggregate rows labelled "Tags" and "Untagged", with ids `__tagged__` and `__untagged__` (labels localized via `tagCollections.getLabel`). The search-side equivalents are `#` and `-#`.
  - Tag colours and icons: the API has `getTagMeta`/`setTagMeta` with `color`, `backgroundColor` and `icon`. The docs do not give UI setting names for tag colours. Feature list: "Folder/tag/property/file colors, icon packs, emoji/Lucide icons, frontmatter read/write, icon mapping by file name and file type category."
  
  **Links and backlinks**
  - No backlink or link features are documented. The wiki backlog mentions them ("Convert to folder note + move all backlinks", "Display local graph on local link hover over") as open requests, not shipped features.
  
  **Folder, tag, property and file icons and colours**
  - Folder colour, background colour and icon are set via `setFolderMeta`. `color: null` clears a value. Icons accept emoji, Lucide slugs and provider-prefixed icons (e.g. `ph-folder`, `si-github`). Values are stored in frontmatter when frontmatter metadata is on (API option `useFrontmatterMetadata`; the UI name is not documented).
  - Folders with their own template show an icon before the note count. The setting "Show folder template icons" turns this off.
  - Wiki backlog (not shipped): "Icon inheritance in tag hierarchy", "Apply tag icon and colors to notes with that tag".
  
  **Shortcuts and pinned items**
  - Shortcuts can be notes, folders, tags, properties, and saved searches, with pinning and reordering. Vault profiles keep per-profile shortcuts.
  - Recent notes/files are stored per vault profile and can be pinned with shortcuts.
  - Commands: "Add to shortcuts", "Open shortcut 1-9", "Toggle pinned section" (shows or hides pinned notes in the list pane).
  - Pinned notes: "Keep important notes at the top of folders and tags." The API has per-context pins (`folder`, `tag`, `property`); a note can be pinned in several contexts.
  - Command "Pin all folder notes" is visible only when folder notes are enabled.
  
  **Search syntax** (filter search, the default mode)
  - Names: `word`, `-word`, and `".F"` for literal text (a term opening with a double quote is never read as a filter).
  - Filters: `has:task`, `-has:task`, `folder:meetings`, `folder:/work/meetings` (no subfolders), `folder:/`, `ext:md` and `ext:.md`, `-ext:pdf`.
  - Dates: `@today`, `@yesterday`, `@last7d`, `@last30d`, `@thisweek`, `@thismonth`, `@2026-02-07`, `@2026`, `@2026-02`, `@2026-W05`, `@2026-Q2`, `@2026-02-01..2026-02-07`, `@c:...` and `@m:...` for created/modified. `-@...` excludes.
  - The default date field follows the sort order. When sorting by name, the date field is set in "Settings → Notes → Date → When sorting by name."
  - AND/OR apply only to tag/property-only queries. If names, dates, task, folder or extension filters are present, `OR` is matched as a file-name word.
  - Omnisearch mode (needs the Omnisearch plugin) is full-text, scoped to the current folder, subfolders or selected tags. It returns at most 50 results.
  - Example combined query from the docs: `meeting .status=active #work @thisweek`.
  
  **Sorting and grouping**
  - "Custom sort and grouping - Override sort/group settings per folder or tag."
  - Manual sort: drag-and-drop, saved to frontmatter. Cmd/Ctrl+Up/Down rearranges in manual sort mode.
  - Folder grouping: groups by parent folder when viewing a folder, tag or property.
  - Date grouping (when sorted by date): Today, Yesterday, Previous 7 days, Previous 30 days, months, years.
  - Property grouping: see the Properties section.
  
  **Custom file-name, preview and date fields from frontmatter**
  - "Name fields" (under Frontmatter) sets which frontmatter field supplies the displayed title. The docs example uses `title`.
  - Previews: 1 to 5 lines, optional HTML stripping. In Omnisearch mode, previews are replaced by Omnisearch excerpts.
  - Note metadata: "Show modification date and tags in the file list."
  - Search date prefixes `@c:` and `@m:` target created and modified dates.
  - Template `{{now}}` produces an ISO 8601 timestamp (default `YYYY-MM-DD[T]HH:mm:ssZ`), which the docs say is "the format Notebook Navigator reads from frontmatter." Use `{{today:YYYY-MM-DD}}` for date properties.
  
  **File-type filters**
  - Search `ext:` and `-ext:` (see Search). File-type icons can be mapped by "file type category." Thumbnails exist for PDF, SVG and drawings. The docs describe no separate file-type filter setting in the navigation pane.
  
  **Hidden folders, tags and properties**
  - "Hidden content" covers folders, tags, notes and files, per vault profile, using patterns, frontmatter properties and tag-based filtering.
  - Command "Toggle hidden folders, tags, and notes" shows or hides them. "Search whole vault" needs "Show root folder" or "Show hidden items" enabled.
  - Wiki backlog (not shipped): "Use ! as a prefix in filters to re-include hidden files/tags/folders."
  
  **Navigation pane sections**
  - The docs name these: folder tree (manual root ordering), tag tree, property browser, shortcuts, recent notes/files, calendar, banner (per vault profile). They do not give exact UI names for the sections or their toggles.
  
  **Dual-pane layout**
  - "Dual-pane layout - Navigation pane (folders/tags/properties) and list pane (files)." Single-pane mode has animated transitions. Panes are resizable, horizontal or vertical.
  - Commands: "Toggle dual pane layout" (desktop and tablet), "Toggle dual pane orientation."
  - Wiki backlog (not shipped): flipping the panes so the folder pane is on the right.
  
  **"Show notes from subfolders"**
  - The UI name used in the docs is "Show notes from subfolders" (in the Omnisearch limits note). The command is "Toggle descendants", suggested as Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+D. "Exclude folders from descendants" omits named folders from subfolder collection, per vault profile.
  - Per-folder/tag appearances include a "descendants toggle."
  
  **Templates that set metadata**
  - Built-in template engine. Tokens include `{{title}}`, `{{folder}}`, `{{path}}`, `{{date}}`, `{{now}}`, `{{today:FORMAT}}`, `{{prompt:Label}}`, `{{number}}` and `{{cursor}}`.
  - Setting names: "Template folder location", "Template engine" (Automatic, Notebook Navigator, Templater), "Trigger Templater on new file creation" (a Templater setting).
  - Folder templates: right-click a folder, "Set folder template...". The closest template wins. Listed under File operations & templates > Templates.
  - Create note commands: under File operations & templates > Create note commands. Each has a name, template, file name format, location and optional ribbon or tab button.
  
  ## Settings, keys and data files
  - Data file: `.obsidian/plugins/notebook-navigator/data.json`. Settings with sync enabled are saved there; settings with sync disabled go to Obsidian local storage.
  - The only `data.json` key the docs describe is `keyboardShortcuts`. Each action maps to a list of `{ "key": ..., "modifiers": [...] }` entries. Example: `"pane:move-up": [ { "key": "ArrowUp", "modifiers": [] }, { "key": "K", "modifiers": [] } ]`.
  - Modifier names: `Mod`, `Alt`, `Shift`, `Ctrl`.
  - Action IDs include `pane:move-up`, `pane:rename`, `navigation:expand-or-focus-list`, `list:manual-sort-up`, `search:close`.
  - Command IDs use the `notebook-navigator:` prefix (e.g. `notebook-navigator:toggle-descendants`, `notebook-navigator:toggle-hidden`, `notebook-navigator:toggle-properties-by-selection`, `notebook-navigator:open-all-files`). The full list is in the README and the docs site.
  - API metadata keys: `color`, `backgroundColor`, `icon`. Property node ids take the form `key:status` and `key:status=done`. Tag ids are stored lowercase without `#`.
  - Pinned storage in the API: `Map<path, { folder, tag, property }>`.
  - Apart from the above, no settings keys are documented. The UI setting names listed in this report are the only ones the docs quote.
  
  ## Setting names quoted in the docs
  "Check for new version on start", "Download external images", "Startup debug logging", "Show folder template icons", "Template engine", "Template folder location", "Name fields", "Trigger Templater on new file creation", "Show notes from subfolders", "Show root folder", "Show hidden items", "Keep selected item expanded", "Auto-reveal active note", "Date format", "Time format", and "When sorting by name" (under Settings → Notes → Date).
  
  ## Gaps
  - The docs do not list the Settings tabs, or the exact UI names for the tag tree, tag colour and icon controls, property browser toggles, navigation sections, sort options or dual-pane settings.
  - No frontmatter key names are documented for storing colours, icons, pins, manual sort order or shortcuts. The docs mention "frontmatter" only in general terms.
  - The wiki Home lists backlog items that are not shipped (e.g. "Dynamic banner from note/folder property", "Use ! as a prefix in filters"). Treat these as unimplemented.
  - Unread: docs/ files other than api-reference.md, FAQ.md, and the wiki's Custom CSS page.
</agent-message>

cat > $SP/apply.py <<'E'
import os,re,yaml,json,sys
SP=sys.argv[1]
ok_tags={'prodos','domain/prodos','prodos/meta','prodos/programme','prodos/prompt'}
def parse(t):
    e=t.find('\n---',3); return yaml.safe_load(t[3:e]) or {}, e
changed=[];skipped=[]
for p in json.load(open(SP+'/targets.json')):
    if p.startswith(('10_System/templates','Excalidraw')): continue
    t=open(p,encoding='utf8').read()
    fm,e=parse(t)
    tg=fm.get('tags') or []; tg=[tg] if isinstance(tg,str) else [str(x).lower() for x in tg]
    match=(set(tg)&ok_tags) or 'prodos' in os.path.basename(p).lower() or str(fm.get('project_name','')).lower()=='prodos'
    if not match or fm.get('project_category') or fm.get('own_words') is True: skipped.append(p);continue
    head=t[:e]; lines=head.split('\n')
    idx=next((i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith('tags:')),len(lines))
    lines.insert(idx,'project_category: prodos')
    new='\n'.join(lines)+t[e:]
    fm2,_=parse(new)
    exp=dict(fm); exp['project_category']='prodos'
    assert fm2==exp,p
    open(p,'w',encoding='utf8').write(new); changed.append(p)
print('changed',len(changed),'skipped',len(skipped))
json.dump(changed,open(SP+'/changed.json','w'))
for p in skipped: print(' skip',p)
E
uv run --with pyyaml python3 $SP/apply.py $SP; git diff --numstat -- $(python3 -c "import json;print(' '.join('\"%s\"'%p for p in json.load(open('$SP/changed.json'))))" | tr -d '"' | head -0) 2>/dev/null | head -0; python3 - <<E
import json,subprocess
c=json.load(open('$SP/changed.json'))
bad=0
for p in c:
    o=subprocess.run(['git','diff','--numstat','--',p],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.split()
    if o[:2]!=['1','0']: bad+=1;print('not 1-line:',p,o[:2])
print('files',len(c),'non-single-line diffs',bad)
E

import yaml
Z='30_Library/100_zettelkasten/'
D={}
def add(name,trigger,steps,verification): D[Z+name+'.md']=(trigger,steps,verification)
add('Archery Shot Process - Nocking','When standing on the shooting line with the bow ready and an arrow to load, before setting the hands',
['Stay in your lane and hold the bow vertical with the lower limb resting against your inner calf','Rest the arrow shaft on top of the arrow rest flipper above the shelf','Click the arrow nock onto the string directly under the brass nocking indicator bead','Turn the fletchings so two hen vanes point toward the bow window and the odd-coloured index vane points away from the riser'],
'The arrow sits on top of the flipper, the nock clicks under the bead every time, and the index vane clears the riser and shelf with no wild flyers or high-low grouping')
add('Archery Shot Process - Stance','At the start of each shot cycle on the shooting line, before building posture',
['Straddle the shooting line with your feet roughly shoulder-width apart in your chosen stance','Keep the hips parallel to the line of your feet for the whole shot','Keep your weight even between front and back foot and bias it about 60/40 onto the balls of the feet','Keep the knees straight but active and not locked','Keep your feet where they are and do not shuffle between arrows'],
'Centre of pressure holds at about 60/40 toe to heel with no rocking onto the heels during expansion, and the feet have not moved between arrows')
add('Archery Shot Process - Posture','After the stance is set and before the hands go on the bow',
['Breathe out fully so the ribcage drops, then hold it down with light abdominal tension','Squeeze the glutes to tuck the pelvis under','Stack shoulders over hips over ankles in one vertical line with no lean toward or away from the target','Look straight at the target with a soft gaze and a neutral neck and keep the head still','Take three long slow breaths to reset before rebuilding posture for the next arrow'],
'In full posture a partner pressing on your upper chest, first steadily and then with a light sudden push, cannot rock you back onto your heels or make you lean into the push')
add('Archery Shot Process - Setup','After posture is set and before raising the bow, when placing the hands on the string and the grip',
['Put on a finger tab or glove and an arm guard','Clear any bulky clothing that could catch the string','Rest the bow on your foot or thigh and not on the long rod while you set up','Hook the string first, placing it in the first joint groove of the middle finger and wrapping the index and ring fingers around it','Roll the fingers in so a pad of flesh sits between the string and the joint and not deep in the knuckle groove','Place the bow hand into the grip last and keep it relaxed'],
'The hook sits on the finger pads without pinching or numbness, the bow hand stays relaxed, and nothing snags the string')
add('Archery Shot Process - Raise','After setup, with hook and grip set, to lift the bow toward eye level before the draw',
['Start relaxed with no continuous tension in the front shoulder','Shift a small amount of weight onto the front foot so the bow shoulder drops','Take up about 1 inch of tension on the string','Raise both hands to eye level while inhaling for four seconds','Rotate the bow arm internally so the elbow turns outward','Reach the base of the bow hand toward the target at the top of the raise','Breathe out and settle downward slightly at the apex','Hold the reach while pulling the string back'],
'The bow shoulder sits down and forward with no locked-out bow elbow, and the reaching tension continues unbroken into the draw')
add('Archery Shot Process - Pre-draw','After the raise and before drawing, as a checklist to confirm alignment',
['Rotate through the core to align the torso for a straight solid connection','Line up the bow wrist, bow shoulder and draw shoulder in one straight line like a rifle barrel','Set the upper draw arm at roughly 90 degrees to the shoulders with the draw elbow on or slightly behind the arrow line','Apply slight tension to the string without aiming yet','Pause briefly and check that the hook and grip have not changed'],
'Posture is tall, the front shoulder stays set down with the acromion divot visible on top of the shoulder, and the bow wrist, bow shoulder and draw shoulder sit in one line')
add('Archery Shot Process - Loading','After the pre-draw checks pass, when drawing the bow to the anchor',
['Start the draw by leading with the back of the drawing shoulder','Move the drawing hand in a clean straight diagonal line toward the lower jaw','Lead the pull with the draw elbow and move the whole drawing shoulder as a unit','Keep the hand limp except for the forearm tension that holds the finger hook static','Draw the remaining length with the back muscles and take the draw elbow up and around','Keep the head still and bring the string to the face','Stop at the load position about half an inch below the jaw','Bring the sight down onto the target from above'],
'The string reaches the face without the head moving forward, the hand travels in a straight line without looping, and the draw stops at the load position about half an inch below the jaw')
add('Archery Shot Process - Anchor','At the end of the draw when the string reaches the face, to fix the final reference point',
['Lift the chin slightly and place the hand on the neck with no gap','Settle into the anchor in one fluid motion straight back','Align the string blur to the same spot each time such as the edge of the riser or beside the sight pin','Keep the front shoulder extended and the core solid','Focus on the target so the bullseye is clear and the sight pin is slightly blurry','Keep the hand where it is if string alignment is slightly off and do not shift it across the face'],
'The same soft tissue and skeletal reference points touch every time, the index finger and bow shelf sit on the same level, and the string blur lands on the same spot')
